sights.address: Bascom Hill, UW–Madison campus, Madison, WI 53706
sights.w: The steep historic quad at the heart of campus, crowned by Bascom Hall and Adolph Weinman's seated Abraham Lincoln — the most-photographed spot for graduating seniors, who climb into his lap. Free.

sights.address: Chamberlin Hall, UW–Madison campus, Madison, WI
sights.w: A 1918 hands-on physics museum — one of the first of its kind — with 65+ interactive exhibits built by faculty and students; free on weekdays.

sights.address: South shore of Lake Mendota, UW–Madison campus, Madison, WI
sights.w: 300 acres along four miles of Lake Mendota's south shore; the Lakeshore Path runs from the Memorial Union through woods and prairie out to Picnic Point. Free.
Wright's 1956 two-room schoolhouse built in honor of his kindergarten-teacher mother, now a cultural arts center a few miles from Taliesin; a stop on Wisconsin's 200-mile Frank Lloyd Wright Trail.

sights.address: 316 S Church St, Richland Center, WI
sights.w: Wright's 1921 Mayan Revival brick-and-concrete warehouse in his birthplace town — the western-most stop on the Frank Lloyd Wright Trail.

sights.address: E9982 Fern Dell Rd (Mirror Lake State Park), Reedsburg, WI
sights.w: One of Wright's last designs, a tiny stone-and-glass cottage over Mirror Lake — the first Wright house anywhere you can rent overnight; open-house tours monthly.
'America's Prettiest Playhouse' — a 1915 Rapp & Rapp movie palace commissioned by circus co-founder Al Ringling; shows, classic films, Barton organ demos and daily 1:30pm tours.

sights.address: SE of Spring Green, Iowa County, WI
sights.w: Small state park on the Wisconsin River bluff with the reconstructed Helena Shot Tower (1832) and its 120-foot shaft through the sandstone; NRHP.
